2610.10062.title: Loud Failures, Quiet Failures: Fault Detection and Recovery in Tool-Using Language Model Agents
2610.10062.paper_summary: Tool-using agents are usually scored on whether they finish a task while the tools work. Deployments are less forgiving: services time out, endpoints disappear, parameter names change, and results come back well formed but wrong. Prior work has shown that language models over-trust tool outputs that fail silently; we ask how that over-trust plays out across the stages of failure handling in multi-turn agents. Wrapping the executable environments of an established function-calling benchmark in a fault-injection layer, we inject one of four typed faults at a controlled point in the trajectory and record whether the agent notices, changes plan, recovers the task, or repeats itself. Six models from three families, half of them reasoning variants, ran 1,920 trials over 24 multi-step tasks. Agents treat a failure as a problem in 91.3% of trials when the tool returns an explicit error, but in 58.8% of trials when it returns a plausible wrong value, against a 26.8% rate of reporting problems when nothing was wrong. Reasoning models are not better placed: paired against instruct siblings, they notice less (-9.3 points, p < .001) and change plan more (+10.4 points, p < .001), and recovery is unchanged (p = .512). Because agents are stochastic, two fault-free runs of the same task end in the same state only 63.3% of the time; against that baseline, only a missing tool clearly lowers recovery (39.9%), while timeouts, schema drift, and corruption stay within run-to-run variation. After a fault, agents return to the same tool three or more times in a row in up to 22.2% of trials, though strictly identical repeats are rare. A prompt line asking the agent to check each result did not move detection. Agents respond to the error channel rather than to the content of what a tool returns, so failures that stay inside the expected format pass through.
2610.10062.paper_summary_zh: 工具使用代理通常根據它們在工具運作時是否完成任務來評分。部署則不那麼寬容：服務會超時，端點會消失，參數名稱會改變，結果雖然格式正確但卻是錯誤的。先前的研究顯示語言模型過度信任靜默失敗的工具輸出；我們詢問這種過度信任如何在多回合代理的失敗處理階段中發揮作用。將一個已建立的函數調用基準的可執行環境包裹在故障注入層中，我們在軌跡中的一個受控點注入四種類型的故障之一，並記錄代理是否注意到、改變計劃、恢復任務或重複自己。來自三個家族的六個模型，其中一半是推理變體，在24個多步任務上進行了1,920次試驗。當工具返回明確錯誤時，代理在91.3%的試驗中將故障視為問題，但當工具返回一個合理的錯誤值時，這一比例降至58.8%，而在沒有任何問題時報告問題的比率為26.8%。推理模型的表現並不更好：與指令兄弟模型相比，它們的注意力更少（-9.3分，p < .001），計劃改變更多（+10.4分，p < .001），而恢復則保持不變（p = .512）。由於代理是隨機的，同一任務的兩次無故障運行只有63.3%的時間結束於相同狀態；與此基準相比，只有缺失工具明顯降低了恢復率（39.9%），而超時、模式漂移和損壞則保持在運行間變異範圍內。在故障之後，代理在最多22.2%的試驗中連續三次或更多次返回相同的工具，儘管完全相同的重複是罕見的。一條提示行要求代理檢查每個結果並未提高檢測率。代理對錯誤通道的反應優於對工具返回內容的反應，因此保持在預期格式內的失敗可以通過。
2610.10062.author: Obada Kraishan et.al.
